attempted_claim: Let Y in P^5 be a general smooth cubic fourfold containing a plane, i.e. a very general member of the Hassett divisor C8, and let F(Y) be its Fano variety of lines, a projective irreducible holomorphic symplectic fourfold of K3^[2]-type with Plucker polarization g satisfying q(g)=6 for the Beauville-Bogomolny-Fujiki form, known to admit a rational Lagrangian fibration F(Y) -> P^2 induced by the plane. Prove or disprove that for general Y in C8 the variety F(Y) itself admits an everywhere-regular holomorphic Lagrangian fibration over P^2. Parameter scope is general, hence very general, smooth cubic fourfolds containing a plane. A complete answer either constructs the regular fibration with explicit isotropic fiber class, base identification, and nefness verification, or proves via Neron-Severi lattice computation, movable/nef-cone analysis, and monodromy-orbit data that general F(Y) admits no holomorphic Lagrangian fibration and the rational fibration cannot be regularized without a Mukai flop.
claim_type: regular versus rational fibration on named family
decisive_failure: The rank-2 lattice certificate verifies e.C=-1 for the movable isotropic ray e but leaves e2.C=+5 open, so the second nefness wall was never established; geometric curve inputs were assumed, not proved; no complete regular-fibration disproof or construction exists.
